title: ORION Capability Registry v1
description: What every tool declares about itself. The live executor keeps its flat action names -- renaming 59 of them would break working prompts, 1000+ ledger rows and the approval hashes that gate re-calls -- so each entry maps one live action onto the structured contract the manifest asks for.

action.description: The live name in catalog.ts. Never renamed by this registry.

capability.description: The manifest's structured name, e.g. calendar.events.read. Two to four dotted segments, narrowing left to right.

domain.description: Which Phase 3 context domain this capability belongs to. Without it the context firewall cannot be applied to a real request, which is why Phase 3's integration waited for this phase. `credentials` is absent on purpose: no capability may belong to it.

side_effects.description: What it changes outside ORION. An empty list means it reads and nothing else, which must be true rather than merely unstated.

resource_scope.description: The narrowest boundary the action can touch. `none` means it reaches no user resource at all.

arguments.description: A real JSON Schema, not a list of names. additionalProperties MUST be false: 'reject unknown fields by default' is the manifest requirement this field exists to satisfy.

returns.description: What the action gives back. Absent before this phase, which is why the Phase 2 bridge had to hand-write system_status's output shape.
